{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overconfidence.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if recent history shows persistent underperformance (e.g., 3+ consecutive forecast errors > 5% below true value).",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent high values (last 5-7 days) when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.00) to capture momentum.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is > 10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 10-20% unless sentiment strongly bullish.",
    "Cap upward forecasts after sharp spikes (e.g., > 15% above prior peak) to avoid overshoot; use sentiment as trigger for decay factor.",
    "If true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (e.g., > 5% over 3 consecutive days), shift model toward higher volatility or upward bias with sentiment weighting.",
    "When sentiment is positive but forecast is low, add 3-5% upward bias to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "For low sentiment periods, apply a 10-15% downward bias to prevent overestimation of price stability."
  ]
}
